implied_side.book: captured consensus (stale) · 1 book · best at DraftKings
implied_side.why: EdgeDesk’s own number sat 8.9 points toward Florida State of the quote EdgeDesk captured at captured consensus (stale) · 1 book · best at DraftKings. That is what the disagreement implied. It was published as research, not as a recommendation to bet it.

implied_total.why: EdgeDesk’s fair total of 50 sat 1.5 points below the captured total of 51.5.

closing_line.why: no closing line is held for this game: the Collective captured none and the schedule feed carries none. Closing-line value is left blank rather than estimated from the result.

reasons: None of the mechanism EdgeDesk named before kickoff could be graded against the statistics published for this game. The scoreboard is not evidence about a mechanism nobody could observe.
process.basis: the drivers, matchups and measured advantages only — never the price or the market claim, which are the result in longer words

variance_markers.label: A 4-turnover swing
variance_markers.text: Clemson Tigers won the turnover battle by 4. Turnover margin is the least repeatable thing in football: it moves scoreboards hard and predicts almost nothing about the next meeting, so a result built on it says less about either team than the scoreline suggests.

verdict.line: The number did not land, in a game the statistics cannot grade the reasoning on. It goes in the record and teaches little.

grading.separation_note: The bet result and the process grade above are computed separately and are allowed to disagree. A winning number with a broken thesis is recorded as exactly that.

lessons.pregame_expectation: 2 published claims said the same thing: EdgeDesk makes it Florida State −8.0 where the market has Florida State +1.5 at captured consensus (stale) · 1 book · best at DraftKings — a 9.3 points disagreement. EdgeDesk prices this game at Florida State −8.0 with a fair total of 49.5, which makes Florida State the better team here by that margin on this field.
lessons.actual_result: Florida State Seminoles lost by 12. Florida State Seminoles lost by 12 where EdgeDesk projected a 7.8-point edge.
lessons.lesson: EdgeDesk named Florida State as better in market and the game went the other way, across 2 separate published claims. One game does not overturn a season-long rating, but this is the direction to watch: the result landed on the market’s side of the disagreement
lessons.suggested_investigation: These claims carried 17.1 points of the published number between them and were contradicted. Check whether the same category has been contradicted in other games this season before touching anything.

lessons.pregame_expectation: 9 of the claims in this article rested on model, passing, rushing, matchup.
lessons.actual_result: None of them could be graded: no single-game statistic in EdgeDesk’s vocabulary observes this driver; the read does not name a side, so there is no direction to test.
lessons.lesson: EdgeDesk prices these games partly on signals it has no way to observe afterwards. That is not an error in the model — it is a gap in the audit, and it means the platform cannot tell, from results alone, whether those parts of the number are earning their weight.
lessons.suggested_investigation: Consider whether a postgame data source exists for model, passing, rushing.

lessons.pregame_expectation: EdgeDesk makes it Florida State −8.0 where the market has Florida State +1.5 at captured consensus (stale) · 1 book · best at DraftKings — a 9.3 points disagreement.
lessons.actual_result: Florida State Seminoles lost by 12. the result landed on the market’s side of the disagreement
lessons.lesson: The market had the better estimate here. EdgeDesk’s disagreement was not information on this game, and the honest reading is that the price already contained what the model thought it had found.
lessons.suggested_investigation: Track disagreements of this size across the season. The question is not whether one landed; it is whether the class of them has any edge at all.
